name: Haiku contrarian turnarounds
strategy: Contrarian recovery in AI-disrupted SaaS (ADBE, CRM down 49%), deeply beaten crypto (BTC/ETH -27-39%), and fintech; expect 2H rebound as market reverses AI-disruption panic, regulatory clarity emerges, and risk-on sentiment persists post-April drawdown.

positions.thesis: Creative Cloud down 49% on AI-disruption fears, but Firefly adoption is accelerating and professional creative tools remain essential. Market panic-sold on unfounded disruption thesis; recovery play on margin expansion as Firefly monetization scales.

Enterprise SaaS down 49% on similar AI-disruption FUD, but Einstein AI is table-stakes now and CRM is mission-critical infrastructure. Market vastly overreacted; recovery play on enterprise software resilience and AI feature adoption.

Deep bear -27.3% H1 on regulatory headwinds, but macro stabilization, SEC ETF approvals, and institutional adoption accelerating. Turnaround catalyst: regulatory clarity (Ripple lawsuit resolution, clearer SEC framework) and crypto winter bottom.
Bitcoin proxy holding significant BTC reserves; leveraged recovery play on BTC bottom. Volatility amplifies upside on crypto stabilization and institutional inflows; 2x+ leverage vs direct BTC.

Block's diversified fintech services (Cash App, Afterpay, Square payments, TBD Bitcoin layer) resilient despite macro concerns. Recovery play on payment volume recovery post-slowdown fears; Bitcoin integration provides long-term optionality.

Ethereum down -36.1%, deeper than BTC, but Layer 2 scaling solutions maturing (Arbitrum, Optimism adoption accelerating) and institutional adoption improving. Turnaround on Ethereum scalability narrative and DeFi recovery.

outlook: Market overreacted to AI-disruption risks in SaaS and regulatory uncertainty in crypto; expect 2H recovery as Firefly/Einstein adoption accelerates, regulatory clarity improves, and institutional risk-on sentiment continues. Outperformance vs SPY if ADBE/CRM and crypto beat post-H1 expectations and mean reversion from overextended semis/Nasdaq flows into beaten-down sectors.
